title: Michael Burry Says Trump Will ‘Pull Out All The Stops’ For AI — ‘Dean Of Valuation’ Holds 5 Mag Seven Stocks, Adds Cash
key_facts: Michael Burry wrote on Substack that the Trump administration will 'pull out all the stops' to protect the AI boom, as it sees AI investment and stocks as 'the best things they have going'.
He warned that backstopping trillions would carry 'epic moral hazard' and that there will be limits to what the administration can do.
He called the fiscal situation 'terrible' and said 'the quiver has fewer arrows this time'.
Aswath Damodaran holds five of the 'Magnificent Seven' stocks (all except Tesla and Nvidia) but put most new money of the past year or two into cash and short-term Treasuries yielding 4%.
Damodaran says a spending-driven rise in aggregate earnings 'comes with an asterisk'; S&P 500 companies returned 63% of earnings via dividends and buybacks, the lowest share since 2004.
He warned of 'both accounting and market carnage' in the worst AI scenarios.
The article also quotes Panmure Liberum's Joachim Klement (bubble bursts in 2027 or 2028) and Goldman Sachs' Christian Mueller-Glissmann (strong tech earnings should continue).
quote_evidence: "But we are talking [about] backstopping trillions with epic moral hazard implications. It will happen but there will be limits as to what they can do in the end," he said.
"A cap-ex driven surge in aggregate earnings comes with an asterisk," he said.
"The tech sector and artificial intelligence theme are still delivering some very strong earnings momentum, and we expect that to continue," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: Two well-known market voices differ on how to hedge against an AI downturn; both are personal opinions.
event_date: 8-9 Oct 2026 (market moves Thursday 8 Oct); date of Burry's Substack post not stated
notes: Yahoo Finance carries a Stocktwits article; Stocktwits is the source. Roundup of opinions; no investment advice given.
